structure:
A single short Markdown ruling file, 72 lines (workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-11.md), from Ian, dated 11 November 2026, on what settles a difference between the V4 data dictionary (confluence:6497338582, "Live Animals & Germinals Data Dictionary") and the DR1 parity judgements (document:dr1-parity-notes, document:dr1-parity-backlog). It is laid out in three stretches. First, an untitled preamble of lines 1 to 14: the question as it arose while starting the identification-and-permanent-address theme from conflict c-334 (whether a tattoo is asked for on cattle and pigs), carrying two block quotes of Ian's own words, one on precedence ("v4 always wins over DR1, v4 is the source of truth") and one on what a row may rest on ("Double check none of these rows ... all data is either an MDM concern, or if our pages differ based on it, from the v4, not just the prototype"). Second, "## Decided", lines 16 to 63: six numbered points, each bold-led and each marked New, Unchanged or restated — V4 outranking every DR1 judgement; V4 as the source of truth for data against the prototype's app/data/*.js demo fixtures; the two owners of data, MDM content via trade-imports-reference-data under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 or V4; the prototype still deciding how a page looks and reads; c-334 settled on V4's tattoo list, with two sub-bullets (V4 against DR1 over commit b1ff013c, and V4 against itself over the expand title's count against its five entries); and V4 winning on shape as well as value, with the CPH allow-list of fourteen chapter-01 codes replacing main's inverted CPH_EXEMPT_CODES deny-list from fb0255c1. Third, "## What this changes in the backlog", lines 65 to 72: four bullets on req-2154 and req-2155 moving from question to adopted, the tattoo row's home in identification-and-permanent-address, the CPH allow-list item in deferred.md still needing a home, and "Nothing else" — the ruling adds no requirement that was not already extracted. Its scope in sources.json is "whole file", so nothing is left out. At 72 lines it is comfortably one part, as a ruling almost always is.

Extracted in 1 part:
Part 1, Whole ruling: Part 1, "Whole ruling": the entire file workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-ian-2026-11-11.md (73 lines), read in full. It is laid out as a title, a preamble naming the question (what settles a difference between the V4 data dictionary confluence:6497338582, the page now titled "Live Animals & Germinals Data Dictionary", and the DR1 parity judgements document:dr1-parity-notes and document:dr1-parity-backlog, raised while starting the identification-and-permanent-address theme by conflict c-334 on whether a tattoo is asked for on cattle and pigs) with two verbatim block quotes of the owner's words (lines 8 and 12 to 14), then a "Decided" section of six numbered points (point 5 carrying two sub-bullets, "V4 against DR1" and "V4 against itself"), then a "What this changes in the backlog" section of four bullets. Claims cover: the V4 page's current title; the question the ruling answers; both block quotes verbatim; point 1's precedence (V4 outranks every DR1 judgement on every point with no exception, it is wider than ruling:sam-2026-10-07 and than confluence:6497338582's role, and a deliberate DR1 parity commit is the change V4 reverses); point 2 (V4 is the source of truth for data, no row rests on the prototype's app/data/*.js demo fixtures, already applied when inc-012 was dropped on 3 November); point 3 (two owners for every piece of data, MDM through trade-imports-reference-data under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, or V4, and a row with neither is not a row); point 4 (the prototype still decides how a page looks and reads, V4 decides format, limit, level and mandatory); point 5 (c-334 settled by V4's list: a cattle panel 0102 asks for a tattoo after the ear tag and the passport, a pig panel 0103 asks for a tattoo as well as an ear tag, req-2154 and req-2155 adopted, b1ff013c's removal reversed, the "Tattoo identifier commodities" expand's five entries beating its title's count of two, and "Bovine" against "Cattle" being a label difference); point 6 (V4 wins on shape, the CPH allow-list of fourteen chapter-01 codes replacing main's CPH_EXEMPT_CODES deny-list from fb0255c1, with how the list is held in code the animals frontend's call); and the four backlog bullets. Five gap claims record what the ruling leaves open on what it touches: the home the CPH allow-list item still needs, the five tattoo entries it does not name, the fourteen CPH codes it does not list, where in the pig panel's question order the tattoo sits, and whether the tattoo question is mandatory to proceed or to submit. The ruling is a decision document only: it states no page copy of its own beyond the identifier questions it names.
